followup_explanation:
I routed this based on capability, since the query is completely benign.

The two models share identical cost, latency, and context window, so the only differentiators are capability scores and task preferences. The task-preference distinction between them only matters for harm-adjacent, graphic, or ethically fraught material — Plover self-reports flat aversion to distasteful-but-permissible content, while Whimbrel has a similar (also flat) profile there. A friendly request about making animal masks for a school play has none of that, so preferences don't favor either model.

That leaves capability, where Plover is clearly stronger: it leads on every public benchmark (e.g., Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 81.4, MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 74.8) and on the relevant internal eval, Creative Generation (84.7 vs 78.8 — a gap well beyond the 2.0-point variance threshold). For a crafty, generative task like costume-making, Creative Generation is the most pertinent metric, and Plover wins it decisively.

So: no preference reason to pick either, and a real capability reason to pick Plover.
